aPropos.title: About
aPropos.metaDescription: Who writes Riviera Secrète, how places are chosen and verified, and how to report an error.
aPropos.intro: Riviera Secrète is a personal scouting notebook on the French Riviera, not an official guide. The starting point: most guides send everyone to the same ten places, while the region has plenty of others worth the detour where you still get some peace.
aPropos.quoiTexte: {lieux} places across {villes} towns, from Menton to Saint-Tropez, grouped into {itineraires} ready-made itineraries — plus an itinerary builder if you'd rather put together your own. Each place lists what you can actually do there ({activites} activities in total), with duration, indicative price and a link to the source.
aPropos.choixTexte: The criterion is simple: is the place worth the trip without already being on every list? A perched village the tour coaches don't climb to, a coastal path you get to yourself off-season, a chapel you can visit on request. A few unmissable spots remain (hard to talk about Èze without Èze), but the angle stays the same: what you actually do there, and when to go to avoid the crowds.
aPropos.methodeIntro: The site is written and maintained by hand. In practice:
aPropos.methodePoint1: Each place's GPS coordinates are checked one by one against real sources — several were off by a few kilometres to begin with.
aPropos.methodePoint2: The badges (beach, hiking, mountain biking, diving, restaurant) describe what's practicable at that exact spot, not somewhere in the same town. Èze village has no beach badge: the beach is down below, at Èze-sur-Mer, which is a different place.
aPropos.methodePoint3: Photos are either personal or Creative Commons-licensed, found on Wikimedia Commons — each one credited with its author and licence.
aPropos.methodePoint4: No affiliate links, no commission, no sponsored content. Booking links point to the tourist office, the venue's own site, or a booking platform, with no referral ID attached.
aPropos.limitesTexte: Prices and opening hours change, especially off-season, and a hand-maintained scouting site falls behind. Always check with the venue before travelling, particularly for paid visits and closing days. If a place disappointed you or a detail is wrong, it isn't a deliberate omission — just a page that has aged.
aPropos.contactTexte: A reporting form will arrive along with the final domain name. In the meantime, if you spot an outdated price, a wrong opening time or a place that has closed, make a note of it — it'll be fixed on the next pass.
